cohort: The study included 133 women aged 20-42 years with a mean gestational age of 37.2 weeks who presented to the OPD or ER with labor pains and initially nonreactive cardiotocography.
finding: Cardiotocography monitoring in labor is associated with a higher risk of caesarean sections due to its high false positive rate, and overweight pregnant women have an increased risk of developing diabetes, premature labor, and preeclampsia, contributing to non-assuring CTG.
mod_finding: C-sections occurred in 43.6% of cases, induction of labor in 31.6% of cases, and cardiotocography monitoring was associated with a higher risk of caesarean sections.
